items.summary: On November 25, 2026, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the First Circuit issued an opinion in Therrien v. Hearst Television, Inc., No. 25-1487, affirming summary judgment for Hearst Television on a Video Privacy Protection Act claim. The plaintiff alleged that Hearst's local news mobile applications disclosed personally identifiable information and video-watching data to Braze, Inc. and Google Ad Manager. The court held that no reasonable juror could find that Hearst violated the statute, and it noted that the district court had found no disclosure of personally identifiable information to either third party and had held that the Braze disclosure fell within the statute's ordinary course of business exception.
